record.paper: Acyclic subgraphs of tournaments with high chromatic number

dossier_meta.paper: Acyclic subgraphs of tournaments with high chromatic number
dossier_meta.statement_text: Every $n$-vertex tournament has an acyclic subgraph with chromatic number at least $n^{3/4-o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(1}\right)}$. That is, $g\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(k}\right)\leq k^{4/3+o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(1}\right)}$.
dossier_meta.context_text: Having established $k^{4/3-o(1)}\leq g(k)\leq k^{9/5+o(1)}$, the authors suspect the lower bound is closer to the truth and propose this conjecture. The lower bound is achieved via a randomized projective-plane construction, and the authors also wonder whether a simpler explicit construction on $n=q^{2}$ vertices attains the same bound.
